$comment: Cases both editors must judge alike. Each case is a source and the issues expected for it, sorted by start, end and code; offsets count UTF-16 code units. An issue without start and end is checked by code only: the two JavaScript parsers do not always place a syntax error on the same character. fixes holds the whole source after each quick fix, in the order offered. The severity and message, where a case gives them, are checked as well. A source here is HTML: each issue is a signal one of its expressions reads that no attribute of the same source declares, as the client stores signals, so the cases hold both editors to the same reads and the same declarations. A case may give prefix, the attribute prefix of an aliased bundle, which is data- otherwise.

cases.name: a signal in the code of a template literal
a signal inside a regular expression is not read
signals in comments are not read
a dollar inside a longer name and in a string is no signal
an attribute name in capitals declares the lowercase key
a capital in a key is lowercased by the browser
a nested object declares its keys under its key
the value of data-bind names the signal as written
a digit after a dollar and a hyphenated signal are no reads to check
an object spread into the object form declares its keys
a spread of something not an object literal, which may declare any signal
a spread of a variable under a key, which declares nothing beside that key
data-ignore: a signal read inside is not the client's
data-ignore: a signal declared inside is never declared
a signal declared after an element with data-ignore is declared
data-ignore nested, on a void element, on an element closed by the next and on a self-closing tag ends with that element
data-star-ignore ends with its element under the alias
